claim: Feature matrix of dotfile managers: chezmoi, dotbot, rcm, vcsh, yadm and bare git compared on Windows support, private files, whole-file encryption, password-manager integration, diffs, templating and run-once scripts.
quote: Windows support: chezmoi ✅, dotbot ✅, rcm ❌, vcsh ❌, yadm ✅, bare git ✅ ... Password manager integration: chezmoi ✅ (others ❌) ... Custom variables in templates: chezmoi ✅ (others ❌)

claim: chezmoi branches per-OS via .chezmoi.os and detects WSL through .chezmoi.kernel.osrelease; on Windows symlink creation needs developer mode or SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege and elevated scripts need Start-Process -Wait.
quote: WSL can be detected by looking for the string `Microsoft` or `microsoft` in /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease ... Symlink creation requires elevated permissions: either enable developer mode or set SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege.

claim: chezmoi pulls secrets at apply time from 1Password, Bitwarden (bw, bws, rbw) and pass, or encrypts committed files with age/gpg, so secrets never live in the dotfiles repo.
quote: chezmoi includes support for Bitwarden using the Bitwarden CLI (bw), Bitwarden Secrets CLI (bws), and rbw to expose data as template functions ... or via encrypted files using age or gpg.

claim: GNU Stow is a Perl symlink-farm manager and depends on the filesystem supporting symbolic links, with no documented Windows support.
quote: a symlink farm manager which takes distinct packages of software and/or data located in separate directories on the filesystem, and makes them appear to be installed in the same place ... a combination of a Perl script providing a CLI interface, and a backend Perl module.

claim: home-manager reaches Windows only through WSL, and symlinks it creates in a Windows directory cannot be read by Windows programs including git and git bash.
quote: Programs from the Windows side cannot read any symlinks, and git and git bash on Windows may give error messages.

claim: home-manager is the Nix-based declarative user-environment manager; it has no native Windows target.
quote: Manage a user environment using Nix.

claim: Hacker News commenters who evaluated Stow and trialled chezmoi report settling on yadm for lower ceremony.
quote: I evaluated Stow and tried Chezmoi for a while but settled on YADM.

claim: Community pain point with yadm is identical content that must live at different paths on different operating systems; yadm covers OS variation only via ##os.Linux / ##os.Darwin alternate files.
quote: While YADM provides support for OS-specific alternatives, users struggle with maintaining identical files that need to reside in different locations on different operating systems.

claim: Definitions for conditional includes (includeIf gitdir/gitdir-i/onbranch/hasconfig) and for core.fileMode, core.symlinks, core.ignoreCase and core.autocrlf.
quote: core.fileMode ... false: Git ignores file mode changes; useful on filesystems that don't properly support permissions (e.g., FAT, NTFS). core.symlinks ... false: Git stores symlink content as regular files; useful on systems with limited symlink support (Windows without special privileges).

claim: Sharing a git working tree on an NTFS partition between Linux and Windows requires uid/gid/dmask/fmask mount options plus core.filemode false and core.ignorecase true, and still produces phantom modifications and ownership conflicts.
quote: UUID=1234-ABCD /mnt/ntfs-share ntfs-3g defaults,uid=YOUR_UID,gid=YOUR_GID,dmask=002,fmask=113 0 0 ... git config --global core.filemode false ... Git incorrectly reports files as modified due to NTFS's inability to preserve executable bits.

claim: git init on an NTFS mount can fail outright because chmod is not permitted on the filesystem.
quote: chmod on /path/on/ntfs/filesystem/myrepo/.git/config.lock failed: Operation not permitted fatal: could not set 'core.filemode' to 'false'

claim: In January 2026 Namjae Jeon posted an 'ntfs filesystem remake' patch series to LKML arguing ntfs3 is poorly maintained, with the replacement passing 308 xfstests versus ntfs3's 235.
quote: ntfs3 still has many problems and is poorly maintained ... passes 308 xfstests compared to ntfs3's 235

claim: Field reports of the in-kernel ntfs3 driver include out-of-memory on large copies, hangs and data loss; blacklisting ntfs3 in favour of the slower ntfs-3g restores reliability.
quote: After blacklisting the ntfs3 kernel module and using ntfs-3g, NTFS problems disappeared, though ntfs-3g is slow but reliable.

claim: 2025 guidance is to stop relying on per-machine core.autocrlf and commit a .gitattributes instead, since only the repo-level file is enforced across machines.
quote: Since core.autocrlf lives on the machine and can't be enforced, the only way to stop line ending issues is to commit a .gitattributes file to the root of your repo.

claim: Git is case-sensitive but Windows and macOS filesystems are not, so checking out File.txt and file.txt on Windows leaves only one file and folders differing only by case get merged.
quote: On Windows and macOS, checking out both "File.txt" and "file.txt" will result in the second one overwriting the first one.

claim: Cloud file-sync clients corrupt git repositories placed inside synced folders; the recommendation is to keep repos outside the sync root.
quote: Cloud syncing services like OneDrive and Dropbox do corrupt Git repositories ... repository corruption is a matter of "when", not "if".

claim: Dropbox's file-sync model lacks the atomicity guarantees git relies on; git-remote-dropbox goes through the Dropbox API rather than the desktop client's file operations and is the safe way to use Dropbox as a remote.
quote: employing the git-remote-dropbox helper tool, which acts as a transparent bridge that interfaces with the Dropbox API rather than relying on the desktop client's file operations

claim: Git Credential Manager uses different credential store backends per OS: wincredman/dpapi on Windows, secretservice (requires a GUI session) or gpg/pass on Linux.
quote: freedesktop.org Secret Service API (secretservice) - Requires a graphical user interface session ... GPG/pass Compatible Files (gpg) - Requires gpg, pass, and a GPG key pair

claim: git-credential-libsecret is the current Linux credential helper; the older libgnome-keyring helper has been deprecated since January 2014.
quote: The best way to store Git credentials on Linux used to be GNOME Keyring (libgnome-keyring), but as it is specific to GNOME, it is deprecated since January 2014. For Git versions 2.11+ you should use credential helper based on libsecret.

claim: PowerShell on Linux stores its profile at ~/.config/powershell/profile.ps1 and lacks COM, Get-WinEvent, Get-CimInstance and the ActiveDirectory module; paths are case-sensitive and .NET Framework modules do not load.
quote: On Linux/macOS, the profile path is located at ~/.config/powershell/profile.ps1 ... Windows-specific modules aren't included in PowerShell for Linux or macOS, and some cmdlets aren't available or might work differently on non-Windows platforms.

claim: A single PowerShell profile can be written to branch on platform so one file serves both Windows and Linux.
quote: Creating a Smarter, Cross-Platform PowerShell Profile

claim: An ed25519-sk resident key (ssh-keygen -O resident, firmware 5.2.3+ with a FIDO2 PIN) stores the credential on the token so the same key works on Windows and Linux without copying a private key.
quote: The -O resident option stores the credential on the key so you can use it across machines ... The handle file does not contain your private key, only a reference that tells OpenSSH which credential on the YubiKey to use; the private key never leaves the hardware.

claim: 2025 best practice is one SSH key per client machine so a leak is attributable and blast radius is limited, rather than copying one private key everywhere.
quote: You should use a separate key per client machine you SSH from, so if a key leaks, you know which client system was compromised.

claim: The 1Password SSH agent serves keys from the vault to git and ssh clients on Windows, macOS and Linux without the client ever reading the private key; an agent config file selects which keys a given machine uses.
quote: It authenticates your Git and SSH clients without those clients ever being able to read your private key, and your private key never even leaves the 1Password app.

claim: Git has supported SSH commit signing since 2.34 via gpg.format=ssh, configured with user.signingkey, commit.gpgsign and gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile, removing the need for GPG agents on both OSes.
quote: git config --global gpg.format "ssh" ... git config gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile "~/.config/git/allowed_signers" ... Git version 2.34 and later supports signing commits and tags with SSH keys — no GPG key needed.

claim: A FIDO2 -sk SSH key can be used to sign git commits, keeping authentication and signing on the same hardware token.
quote: Securing git with SSH and FIDO2

claim: VS Code Settings Sync covers settings, keybindings, snippets, tasks, UI state, extensions and profiles; keybindings sync per platform by default and machine-scoped settings are excluded.
quote: Machine settings (with `machine` or `machine-overridable` scopes) are not synchronized by default, since their values are specific to a given machine ... Keyboard Shortcuts are synchronized per platform by default.

claim: Rider's Backup and Sync plugin is bundled and enabled by default and syncs themes, keymaps, colour schemes, editor and code-style settings, live templates and the enabled-plugin list under a JetBrains Account.
quote: Rider can back up and sync settings between IDE instances via the Backup and Sync plugin, which stores data under a JetBrains Account, making synced settings available in all IDEs where you log in with that account.

claim: Microsoft retired the native Teams desktop client for Linux and replaced it with a progressive web app.
quote: Microsoft Decides to Drop the Linux App for Teams to Replace it as a Progressive Web App Instead

claim: Firefox Sync is end-to-end encrypted and syncs extension settings and data, which Chrome does not; Chrome and Firefox sync payloads are cryptographically incompatible.
quote: Firefox syncs extension settings and data, while Chrome doesn't ... Chrome sync data is cryptographically incompatible with Firefox's protocol.

claim: dotnet user-secrets writes to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\UserSecrets\<id>\secrets.json on Windows and ~/.microsoft/usersecrets/<id>/secrets.json on Linux/macOS — per-user, per-OS, outside the project.
quote: On Windows, user secrets are stored at: %APPDATA%\Microsoft\UserSecrets\<user_secrets_id>\secrets.json, while on Linux/macOS they are stored at: ~/.microsoft/usersecrets/<user_secrets_id>/secrets.json

claim: The NuGet global packages folder defaults to %userprofile%\.nuget\packages on Windows and ~/.nuget/packages on Linux/macOS, overridable via NUGET_PACKAGES.
quote: The default NuGet global packages folder is %userprofile%\.nuget\packages on Windows or ~/.nuget/packages on Mac/Linux ... The NUGET_PACKAGES environment variable overrides the default location and takes precedence.

claim: global.json pins which .NET SDK the CLI uses, requires a full version number, offers rollForward policies such as latestFeature, and since .NET 10 supports a paths array (e.g. [".dotnet", "$host$"]) plus a custom errorMessage for repo-local SDKs.
quote: The global.json file allows you to define which .NET SDK version is used when you run .NET CLI commands ... paths - Available since: .NET 10 SDK. Specifies the locations that should be considered when searching for a compatible .NET SDK ... The special value $host$ represents the location corresponding to the running dotnet executable.

claim: The Development Containers specification is an open standard where devcontainer.json describes the whole development environment — OS, runtime, tools, settings — as code, supported by a range of tools rather than one vendor.
quote: an open specification for enriching containers with development specific content and settings ... a variety of tools and services support this standard

claim: Microsoft documents dev containers as the way to try new .NET SDK releases without altering the host machine's installation.
quote: Exploring new .NET releases with Dev Containers

claim: Under WSL2, files accessed through /mnt/c cross a Linux/Windows boundary and run roughly 2x to 10x slower; git is disproportionately affected because it stats many files.
quote: Performance degradation can range from 2x slower to 10x slower, and in some cases it can be worse ... Git scans directories, checks metadata, and compares file states—on a slow filesystem bridge, this becomes painfully obvious.

claim: Long-running upstream issue tracking WSL2 filesystem performance in /mnt being much slower than WSL1.
quote: [wsl2] filesystem performance is much slower than wsl1 in /mnt
